meta.title: Major regime and constitutional transitions outside Europe, 1836–2026
meta.scope: Selected major regime changes, independence, coups, republic/monarchy transitions, one-party consolidation, constitutional transitions and major state re-foundations in the Middle East/North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and Asia. Not an exhaustive country-year regime dataset.
meta.schemaNote: Uses the CG-41 event schema exactly: id, date, capitalHistorical, entityBefore, entityAfter, eventType, causes, lawChanges, territorialChanges, sources, quality, note; optional windowStart/windowEnd. Law group values are restricted to the current engine LawGroup and REFORMABLE_LAWS enums. Proposed historical entity IDs are research identifiers, not guaranteed registry IDs.
meta.dateConvention: ISO-8601 Gregorian. A date is the principal legal/proclamation milestone; for transitions extending over time, note the process in the event note. Do not infer instant territorial control from a regime proclamation.

qualityLegend.verified: Primary law, official government, UN or official archive directly confirms the date/legal act.
qualityLegend.supported: Credible academic or institutional synthesis supports the date and interpretation; some detail remains approximate.

coverageLimitations: This is a high-salience chronology, not a complete list of all coups, cabinet changes, electoral turnovers, constitutional amendments or civil wars.
Some events mark leadership changes within a continuing regime (e.g. Nasser/Assad) and should not be treated as changes in state form.

Some engine law mappings are deliberately conservative approximations; see each lawChanges.note. In particular, one_party_state is a gameplay abstraction for hegemonic-party rule in cases where opposition parties were not formally banned.
Events dated to a year or broad process should not be promoted to day-level precision without further primary-source review.
Syria's post-December 2024 transition is still in progress as of the research date; the March 2025 declaration is transitional, not a permanent constitution.

The date range is 1836–2026, but the latest included high-salience regime transition is Syria's 13 March 2025 transitional constitutional declaration. No 2026 regime-change milestone was added without a substantiated qualifying event; the absence of a 2026 event is not a claim that no political developments occurred.
meta.capitalCoordinateExtension: Optional capitalCoordinates are approximate WGS84 city points added as integration hints because the current build-regimes.ts CITY table does not cover these non-European capitals. Claude must independently verify each map-grid lookup and must not treat coordinates as a political-region assignment.
